div.div:
Little's Law Calculation:
L = λ × W = 1,000 req/sec × 0.050 sec = 50 concurrent threads
• Mean Latency: 50ms | Thread Utilization: 25% | Queue Delay: 0ms

div.div:
System Behavior:
The service smoothly absorbs fluctuations. Threads return instantly to the idle pool upon
downstream response. Requests complete with sub-second turnaround.

div.div:
Little's Law Demand vs Pool Ceiling:
Required L = λ × W = 1,000 req/sec × 0.500 sec = 500 threads needed
Deficit: +300 threads beyond hard pool capacity (Saturates in < 300ms)

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 392px; margin-left: 594px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #334155;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Comic Sans MS'; color: light-dark(#334155, #acb8c9); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: nowrap;

div.div:
Cascading Failure Mechanics:
1. Sockets queue on OS TCP backlog until net.core.somaxconn overflows.
2. Inbound requests are dropped or rejected with HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout.
3. Upstream API Gateway exhausts its own thread pool waiting on Order Service.
The entire synchronous topology collapses from a single edge latency hiccup.
